instruction: telemetry.py keeps its counters and gauges in module-level dictionaries, so a program cannot keep two independent sets of metrics (one per tenant, say, or one per test). Restructure it around a Registry class: Registry() holds its own state and has methods increment, counter, set_gauge, gauge, snapshot and reset with the same signatures and behaviour as today's module functions. The module exposes default_registry, a Registry instance, and keeps every existing module-level function, including the track_calls decorator, with the same names, signatures and behaviour. Those functions, and functions decorated with track_calls, act on whichever registry telemetry.default_registry refers to at the moment they run. No module-level dict, list or set may remain. tests/test_telemetry.py checks this; don't modify it.
